doc.title: Joe Darensbourg and Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1957-04-18

title: Charlie Creath's big band at the Plantation on Market Street
summary: He describes Creath's nine- or ten-piece reading band with stock arrangements at the big St. Louis club.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, I'll tell them, tell us about St. Louis.
When did you play with him? Well, this is, uh, the latter part of 26.
Did you play saxophone player? I played both then. Both. Did you play on both for the stage? Mostly, yeah.
Mostly, mostly both, but we played a lot of, yeah, excursions.

And we played, uh, we played different gigs. It wasn't no steady job. Now, Charlie Crefft's job, Charlie Crefft had this club, this plantation on Market Street. Mm-hmm. In St. Louis? Yeah, in St. Louis. Uh, it was right down the street from the old Book of Washington Theater.
Yeah. Now, Marge wasn't with Charlie Crefft at that time, was it?

Well, no, I wouldn't know. You know Marge? Yeah, yeah. His sister? I wouldn't, I wouldn't know. Who married Zuri? Yeah, yeah. No. I don't know, because I never met, uh, I didn't meet his wife, uh, in fact, I can't even remember one guy that was in that band. Hmm. It was a big, it was a fairly big band for those days. Did you play in that band yourself? Yeah. It was about, uh, uh, nine or ten pieces. They had two, three saxophones in that band, and you read everything then.
You read it? Oh, yeah. In Charlie Crefft's band? Yeah. For the reading band? Well, sure. Nine or ten pieces? Naturally.
They had, they had, they had orchestrations, the score. Uh-huh. Stock arrangements then. Uh-huh. They never had any specials. Uh-huh.
Yeah, because, uh, what kind of business did I take?
Well, it was a real, it was a big club. Big club? Oh, yeah. Yeah, dancing, and we played on a kind of, uh, an elevated, uh, balcony, like. We played, uh, afternoons and night.
But where'd you go to advertising? Advertising? Where'd you, what part of the town would you go to for that? Well...
